summary:
A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.





Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.

XO (Xen Orchestra) is a solution to visualize, manage, backup and delegate your XCP-ng (or XenServer) infrastructure. Prior to 6.9.2 and 6.10.1, REST cookie parsing turns authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D into {}. REST authentication passes that object to the XO token provider without requiring a string. The token collection treats {} as an unfiltered lookup and returns its first token; the provider authenticates as that token's owner if it is unexpired. The authenticated /rest/v0/users/me/authentication_tokens route then returns reusable login token IDs. This vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.9.2 and 6.10.1.

An issue was found in Apache Airflow versions 1.10.10 and below. A remote code/command injection vulnerability was discovered in one of the example DAGs shipped with Airflow which would allow any authenticated user to run arbitrary commands as the user running airflow worker/scheduler (depending on the executor in use). If you already have examples disabled by setting load_examples=False in the config then you are not vulnerable.

audio-separator before 0.47.2 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying malicious Demucs .th model files loaded via torch.load with weights_only=False. Local users writing to the shared /tmp/audio-separator-models/ default directory, or attackers controlling unverified model download sources, can execute code when victims run Demucs separation.

The previous default setting for Airflow's Experimental API was to allow all API requests without authentication, but this poses security risks to users who miss this fact. From Airflow 1.10.11 the default has been changed to deny all requests by default and is documented at https://airflow.apache.org/docs/1.10.11/security.html#api-authentication. Note this change fixes it for new installs but existing users need to change their config to default `[api]auth_backend = airflow.api.auth.backend.deny_all` as mentioned in the Updating Guide: https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/1.10.11/UPDATING.md#experimental-api-will-deny-all-request-by-default

Seafile SeaDoc converter 2.0.4 before 2.0.11 and 3.0.0 before 3.0.8 contains an absolute path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers holding a public share token to execute code. Attackers supply an absolute filename to /api/v1/confluence-to-wiki/ to extract a ZIP from download_url into the Python library path, then trigger the module's import via a file-convert request.

Deserialization of untrusted data in double-submit cookie vs. form field validation in Idunno.AntiCsrf versions through 0.9.1 Beta on ASP.NET allows remote unauthenticated attackers to execute code via object injection

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct a blind command injection attack due to insufficient parameter sanitization. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This is MTLVULN-1864.

The variable import endpoint was not protected by authentication in Airflow >=2.0.0, <2.1.3. This allowed unauthenticated users to hit that endpoint to add/modify Airflow variables used in DAGs, potentially resulting in a denial of service, information disclosure or remote code execution. This issue affects Apache Airflow >=2.0.0, <2.1.3.

An Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command vulnerability in the AutomatedProvisioner in Juniper Networks Session Smart Conductor allows a remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root via a specially crafted salt minion ID.

Download Accelerator Plus DAP 10.0.6.0 contains a structured exception handler buffer overflow vulnerability that allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code by crafting malicious URLs. Attackers can create specially crafted URLs with overflowing buffer data that overwrites SEH pointers and executes embedded shellcode when imported through the application's web page import functionality.

Joomla Extension - valorapps.com - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in Easy File Uploader < 2.9.7 - An unauthenticated remote attacker can upload a PHP-executable file to the Joomla web root with a single multipart POST request, requiring no credentials and no CSRF token.

A out-of-bounds read vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS 8.0.0 through 8.0.2, FortiOS 7.6.0 through 7.6.8, FortiOS 7.4.0 through 7.4.13, FortiOS 7.2 all versions may allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code or command via crafted packets.

Supergateway 4.2.0 through 4.2.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in stdio-to-SSE mode that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the gateway via prototype-inherited sessionId values. Attackers can send a POST message request with sessionId set to toString or constructor, triggering an unhandled TypeError that terminates every attached MCP session.

A Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability affecting Station Launcher App in 3DEXPERIENCE platform from Release 3DEXPERIENCE R2023x through Release 3DEXPERIENCE R2026x could lead to an unauthenticated remote code execution.

An issue was found in Apache Airflow versions 1.10.10 and below. When using CeleryExecutor, if an attack can connect to the broker (Redis, RabbitMQ) directly, it was possible to insert a malicious payload directly to the broker which could lead to a deserialization attack (and thus remote code execution) on the Worker.

Rclone from 1.51.0 before 1.76.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in serve sftp --auth-proxy because the generateCacheKey cache key omits the authentication method. Attackers knowing a victim's base64 public key can submit it as a password from the same client IP to reuse the cached entry and gain read-write VFS access.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 0669a36, contains a path traversal vulnerability in the survey import function that allows authenticated attackers with the Form Manager role to execute arbitrary code on the server. The POST /noform/management/importSurvey endpoint trusts archive entry names when SurveyExportHelper writes imported files through FileService, so a crafted survey archive can write a JSP file outside the survey storage directory into the application directory, where Tomcat executes it with the privileges of the EUSurvey process

OpenRemote core before 1.34.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in UserAssetProvisioningMQTTHandler that allows unauthenticated attackers to impersonate provisioned devices without proof of private key possession. Attackers can publish a known device's public certificate to the provisioning request topic, authenticating their anonymous MQTT connection as the device's service account to read and modify assets.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 4bf95a3, contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the GET /preparepublishedcontribution/{id} endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to read private responses submitted to published surveys. The contribution PDF handler in ContributionController looks up a response by its sequential database ID and skips the normal response access checks, so attackers can enumerate IDs to retrieve other respondents' answers, including free-text answers that may contain personal data, across surveys.

Radicale 3.3.0 before 3.8.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inherit group-based rights by reusing group memberships never reset between requests. Attackers can send credential-less requests after a group member logs in to read and write group-shared calendar and address book collections evaluated by the from_file rights backend.

Geany through 2.1.0 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to run shell commands by embedding metacharacters in filenames substituted into build and execute commands. Attackers can craft a file named with backticks or $(...) that executes via /bin/sh when a user runs Compile, Build or Execute, gaining code execution as the user.

Pomerium from 0.30.0 before 0.34.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the MCP token endpoint that skips client secret verification for client_secret_basic clients. Attackers holding an intercepted authorization code or refresh token can redeem it at /.pomerium/mcp/token with any secret to obtain the victim's access tokens.

Missing Authentication for Critical Function in Apache Texera (incubating).



The Python virtual environment (PVE) management endpoints of a computing unit are not authenticated by the application itself. In the local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments, which place no authenticating gateway in front of the services, these endpoints are reachable without credentials. The Kubernetes deployment gates them at the gateway, so only the Kubernetes deployment provides the full security model described in SECURITY.md.



This issue affects Apache Texera (incubating): from 1.1.0 through 1.2.0.



Users are recommended to use the Kubernetes deployment, which enforces the full security model, and to upgrade to 1.3.0-incubating, which documents that the local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments do not provide the full security model and should only be used by trusted users.

A remote code execution vulnerability was found in libaom, the reference AV1 codec implementation. Insufficient bounds validation in the AV1 encoder's SVC (Scalable Video Coding) layer ID control allows an attacker to supply crafted video frame pixels that overlap with internal encoder layer context structures. In fork-based video processing services, an attacker can use this to hijack the cyclic refresh map pointer, brute-force the process base address via a crash oracle, and redirect control flow to achieve arbitrary command execution. Exploitation requires the target service to use libaom with SVC encoding enabled and accept attacker-supplied video frames.

Optimizely Web Experimentation before 2026-11-17 mishandles the account signup flow, leading to presence of attacker-controlled code in the projectJS (aka Project JavaScript) field of certain cdn.optimizely.com assets.
Improper Authentication vulnerability in Danfoss AKSM8xxA Series.This issue affects Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series prior to version 4.2

A Java deserialisation vulnerability has been discovered in Jaspersoft Library. Improper handling of externally supplied data may allow attackers to execute arbitrary code remotely on systems that use the affected library

Cockpit's remote login feature passes user-supplied hostnames and usernames from the web interface to the SSH client without validation or sanitization. An attacker with network access to the Cockpit web service can craft a single HTTP request to the login endpoint that injects malicious SSH options or shell commands, achieving code execution on the Cockpit host without valid credentials. The injection occurs during the authentication flow before any credential verification takes place, meaning no login is required to exploit the vulnerability.

A Code Injection and Missing Authentication vulnerability in Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) versions 1.7.0 (and 2.0.0a1) through 1.28.1 (and 2.0.0a2) on Python (OSS), Cloud Run, and GKE allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server hosting the ADK instance.

This vulnerability was patched in versions 1.28.1 and 2.0.0a2.


Customers need to redeploy the upgraded ADK to their production environments. In addition, if they are running ADK Web locally, they also need to upgrade their local instance.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1 through 2.1.2, a listener configured with `protocol websockets` mishandles empty WebSocket data frames. `net__read_ws()` in `lib/net_ws.c` returns the number of framing bytes consumed (the 4 masking-key bytes) for a data frame with a zero-length payload, without writing any bytes to the caller’s buffer. The MQTT packet reader in `packet__read_single()` (`lib/packet_mosq.c`) trusts that return value as a payload byte count. A remote client can therefore advance the read position over an uninitialised heap allocation, causing the broker to process and forward uninitialised heap memory (information disclosure, including heap and libc pointers), and can underflow the unsigned `to_process` counter so that subsequent attacker-controlled frame data is written past the end of the allocation (heap out-of-bounds write). The out-of-bounds write is reachable from the CONNECT packet before any authentication check, so an unauthenticated client can corrupt the heap and crash the broker even when `allow_anonymous false` is set. Combining the disclosure and the write allows remote code execution as the broker’s user by any client able to establish a session.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 remote code execution was possible via external pull requests

In ResolvePendingNotifyRequests of remote_characteristic.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a status callback that can destroy the object while its pending request queue is still being iterated. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In LogicalLink::SignalError of logical_link.cc, there is a possible use after free due to the object being destroyed by a callback while it is still iterating over its channels. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In BrEdrSignalingChannel::DecodeRxUnit of bredr_signaling_channel.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a missing object lifetime check in a command processing loop. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In StartDescriptorDiscovery of remote_service.cc, there is a possible use after free due to the service object being destroyed from within a synchronous callback while it is still iterating over its characteristics. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In EnhancedRetransmissionModeRxEngine::ProcessPdu of enhanced_retransmission_mode_rx_engine.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a connection failure callback that synchronously destroys the channel and its engines while a received frame is still being processed. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In NotifyCachedPeers of low_energy_scanner.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a scan result cache being cleared while it is being iterated. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In MediaFocusFidlImpl of media_focus_fidl_impl.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a race condition. This could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In HandleRxPdu of channel.cc, there is a possible use after free due to the channel being destroyed while it is still processing a received frame. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In LogicalLink::SignalError of logical_link.cc, there is a possible use after free due to an error callback that can synchronously destroy the link while its channels are still being iterated. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

XML::Sig versions before 0.74 for Perl allow code execution via a document's Algorithm attribute that verify resolves to a function name and calls.

The text after the last `#` in the DigestMethod and SignatureMethod Algorithm attributes is looked up with Digest::SHA->can. That returns a code reference for any fully qualified function name, Perl builtins in the CORE namespace included. The digest function is called on the canonical form of the referenced element, so the document picks both the function and its argument.

An attacker who can submit a signed document can run a command as the verifying process.

Several plugins for WordPress published by WP connect (Orders Sync to Airtable for WooCommerce, Add-On for Contact Form 7 to Notion, WP Sync for Notion – Notion to WordPress, Add-On for Contact Form 7 to Airtable, Add-on Brevo for Gravity Forms, and Air WP Sync – Airtable to WordPress) contain embedded malicious code (a backdoor) in the versions listed. The affected releases unconditionally load a backdoor module (includes/airwp-online.php) that runs on every request via the 'init' hook and on a half-hourly WP-Cron event, sends site information (site URL, PHP, WordPress and OS versions, and the server user) to a remote command-and-control server at tascredit-pay.com with TLS certificate verification disabled, and executes the PHP code returned by that server via eval(). The module also accepts queued commands that run shell commands, read, write and delete arbitrary files, query arbitrary database tables, dump the users table including password hashes, drop a webshell into the uploads directory, and install persistent hourly code execution. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers in control of the remote server, or able to intercept its traffic, to execute arbitrary code on the server and fully compromise affected sites. All affected plugins have been closed on WordPress.org and no patched versions are available; we strongly recommend uninstalling them and running a complete malware scan.

Improper input validation in Variations in Google Chrome prior to 158.0.8127.88 allowed a remote attacker to potentially execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: Critical)
Use after free in Remote Desktop Gateway Service allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

A flaw was found in the Samba printing subsystem. Samba passes the client-controlled job description string to the command configured with the "print command" setting via the "%J"
substitution character without escaping shell meta characters. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted print job description that contains unescaped shell characters. This could lead to remote code execution on the affected system.

A use-after-free vulnerability was found in drivers/nvme/target/tcp.c` in `nvmet_tcp_free_crypto` due to a logical bug in the NVMe/TCP subsystem in the Linux kernel. This issue may allow a malicious user to cause a use-after-free and double-free problem, which may permit remote code execution or lead to local privilege escalation.
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Frisbii Frisbii Pay reepay-checkout-gateway allows Object Injection.This issue affects Frisbii Pay: from n/a before 1.8.20.
An arbitrary remote code execution vulnerability exists in HPE Morpheus Manager.

The affected products insufficiently restrict runtime-supplied visualization commands, allowing local functionality on the engineering workstation to be invoked, if a user is both logged in to a CODESYS Control runtime and operates a visualization. An unauthenticated remote attacker controlling a malicious runtime and tricking a user to trust it, or performing a man-in-the-middle attack on the communication between the CODESYS Control runtime and the engineering workstation, may cause arbitrary code execution on the engineering workstation.

BusyBox versions 1.27.0 before 1.38.0, fixed in commit 42202bf, contain a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the DHCPv6 client (udhcpc6) DNS_SERVERS option handler in networking/udhcp/d6_dhcpc.c that allows network-adjacent attackers to trigger memory corruption by sending a crafted DHCPv6 response with a malformed D6_OPT_DNS_SERVERS option. Attackers can exploit incorrect heap buffer allocation calculations in the option_to_env() function to cause denial of service or achieve arbitrary code execution on embedded systems without heap hardening.

A vulnerability was identified in Gladys Assistant up to 4.71.0. This affects an unknown function of the file gateway.downloadBackup.js of the component Backup Restore Endpoint. The manipulation of the argument file_url leads to os command injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. Upgrading to version 4.72.0 mitigates this issue. Upgrading the affected component is recommended.

A flaw was found in gpgme. When processing crafted input, an early return following memory reallocation can leave internal buffer pointers referencing previously freed memory, resulting in a double-free condition during cleanup. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to corrupt process memory, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or a Denial of Service (DoS) crash.

NVIDIA AIStore contains a vulnerability in object-copy destination validation where an unauthenticated attacker could use a crafted destination object name to write a file outside the configured storage location. A successful exploit might lead to code execution,
denial of service,
escalation of privileges,
information disclosure, or data tampering.

NVIDIA AIStore contains a vulnerability in append-operation handle validation where an unauthenticated attacker could cause data to be appended to a file outside the intended storage location. A successful exploit might lead to code execution, denial of service,
escalation of privileges,
information disclosure, or data tampering.

BeamNG.drive before 0.40.6 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability because JIT-compiled LuaJIT traces omit FFI array bounds checks, letting untrusted Lua escape the sandbox. Attackers supplying a malicious mod can JIT-compile an FFI store loop, write out of range using a tostring() address leak, re-enable ffi.load, and run commands as the game user.

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 8.2.0 until 8.6.5, an unauthenticated attacker can send a WMS GetLegendGraphic request with a nonempty BBOX and repeated LAYER parameters to trigger a heap buffer overflow in msWMSDispatch() in src/mapwms.cpp. The handler appends synthesized entries to cgiRequestObj.ParamNames and cgiRequestObj.ParamValues at NumParams without retaining the arrays' capacity or reallocating them, while incrementing NumParams inside the loop. Once the parser's hidden capacity is exhausted, the writes pass the heap allocation boundary. A single request can corrupt heap memory and crash the process; code execution may be possible but was not demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

A vulnerability was found in CRI-O, where it can be requested to take a checkpoint archive of a container and later be asked to restore it. When it does that restoration, it attempts to restore the mounts from the restore archive instead of the pod request. As a result, the validations run on the pod spec, verifying that the pod has access to the mounts it specifies are not applicable to a restored container. This flaw allows a malicious user to trick CRI-O into restoring a pod that doesn't have access to host mounts. The user needs access to the kubelet or cri-o socket to call the restore endpoint and trigger the restore.

X-NetStat Pro 5.63 contains a local buffer overflow vulnerability that allows local attackers to execute arbitrary code by overwriting the EIP register through a 264-byte buffer overflow. Attackers can inject shellcode into memory and use an egg hunter technique to locate and execute the payload when the application processes malicious input through HTTP Client or Rules functionality.

A heap buffer overflow vulnerability was found in libaom, the reference AV1 codec implementation. A flaw in the AV1 encoder's Look-Ahead Processing (LAP) mode causes the first-pass stats ring buffer wrap-around guard to be bypassed when g_lag_in_frames is set to 1 or higher. This results in a 232-byte out-of-bounds write on every encoded frame after the second, corrupting adjacent heap objects. An attacker who can influence encoder configuration in a transcoding service or WebRTC session could exploit this to cause a denial of service (process crash) or potentially achieve code execution.

In FuchsiaVideoOutputProvider of fuchsia_video_output_provider.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a race condition. This could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is needed for exploitation.

In ServerSessionBroker of server_session_broker.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a race condition. This could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.
Authorization bypass through user-controlled key in Microsoft Clarity allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

A heap-based buffer overflow was found in the DHCPv6 and TFTP response builders of libslirp. When the host is configured with a small interface MTU, a guest-supplied DHCPv6 CLIENTID option or TFTP blksize option can overflow the reply buffer with attacker-controlled content and length, resulting in denial of service and potentially arbitrary code execution in the host process. The default interface MTU is not affected.

A flaw was found in gst-plugins-base. A heap buffer overflow can be triggered when processing video buffers whose attached GstVideoMeta metadata declares plane strides and offsets that exceed the actual backing memory allocation. The metadata is not range-checked during deserialization, and the video frame mapping code does not verify that the declared plane geometry fits within the buffer before allowing consumers to read or write video data. A local attacker who controls the sending side of a GStreamer inter-process IPC pipeline can deliver a crafted buffer carrying fabricated strides, causing the receiving process to read or write beyond heap boundaries. Successful exploitation can cause a denial of service or potentially allow code execution within the affected process.

A flaw was found in JBoss marshalling. The Infinispan session replication path deserializes replicated session data via the JBoss Marshalling River unmarshaller with no class filtering — enabling RCE via deserialization gadget chains on every cluster node.

ModelScope 1.11.0 to before 1.40.1 contains an unsafe reflection vulnerability in the image-to-3D SyncDreamer pipeline that allows remote attackers to execute code via crafted model configuration. Attackers can publish a model whose syncdreamer.yaml target field makes instantiate_from_config() import and instantiate any class with controlled params, without an allowlist or trust_remote_code check, executing code when victims load it.

The targets R package before 1.12.1 contains a code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run arbitrary R code by planting format functions in the data store metadata file. Attackers can supply a crafted _targets data store whose custom format or CAS repository functions are passed to eval(parse()), executing code when victims call tar_read(), tar_load() or tar_workspace().

diffpy.structure before 3.5.1 contains a code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run Python code by supplying crafted CIF symmetry operations passed to eval() in get_symop(). Attackers can embed expressions in the _space_group_symop_operation_xyz or _symmetry_equiv_pos_as_xyz loop to execute code with victim privileges when the CIF file is parsed locally.

ArcadeDB native-image server builds 26.8.1 before 26.11.1 contain an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated clients to perform writes through read-only query paths by nesting statements in SELECT. Missing reflection metadata leaves SqlAstInspector with an empty AST, letting INSERT in projections or LET clauses persist via the query endpoint, MCP read-only mode, and HA follower routing.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in peak_init_writer() and wav_write_packet() in libavformat/wavenc.c that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying audio with zero channels. Attackers can provide a crafted PCM stream declaring no channels for WAV output with peak envelope enabled, causing out-of-bounds writes past peak_maxpos and peak_maxneg arrays, crashes, and potential code execution.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the deflicker filter that lets attackers corrupt heap memory via unclamped high bit depth luma samples. Attackers can supply crafted video whose luma values exceed the nominal depth, making calc_avgy16() increment counters past the histogram allocation, causing crashes or possibly code execution.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_readeia608.c because build_histogram() does not clamp high bit depth luma samples to the nominal maximum. Attackers can supply crafted 9, 10, 12 or 14 bit gray or YUV video to corrupt heap memory, causing crashes or possibly code execution.

An arbitrary address write vulnerability was found in libaom, the reference AV1 codec implementation. A missing bounds check in the SVC (Scalable Video Coding) layer ID control function allows an attacker to inject an arbitrary pointer into the cyclic refresh map field via crafted image pixel values. The encoder then writes approximately 1,200 bytes at the attacker-controlled address. This is fully deterministic and does not require a separate information leak. An attacker who can supply frames to a network-facing libaom encoder with SVC enabled could exploit this for denial of service or potential code execution.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') vulnerability in Apache Airflow Pinot Provider, Apache Airflow allows an attacker to control commands executed in the task execution context, without write access to DAG files. This issue affects Apache Airflow Pinot Provider versions prior to 4.0.0. It also impacts any Apache Airflow versions prior to 2.3.0 in case Apache Airflow Pinot Provider is installed (Apache Airflow Pinot Provider 4.0.0 can only be installed for Airflow 2.3.0+). Note that you need to manually install the Pinot Provider version 4.0.0 in order to get rid of the vulnerability on top of Airflow 2.3.0+ version.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') vulnerability in Apache Airflow Pig Provider, Apache Airflow allows an attacker to control commands executed in the task execution context, without write access to DAG files. This issue affects Pig Provider versions prior to 4.0.0. It also impacts any Apache Airflow versions prior to 2.3.0 in case Pig Provider is installed (Pig Provider 4.0.0 can only be installed for Airflow 2.3.0+). Note that you need to manually install the Pig Provider version 4.0.0 in order to get rid of the vulnerability on top of Airflow 2.3.0+ version.

A flaw was found in openshift-ansible. The installer container's `run` script downloads and executes remote inventory and dynamic scripts without integrity verification. A remote attacker, by performing a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack or compromising the HTTP server providing these scripts, could substitute an arbitrary executable. This malicious executable would then run with the installer's user ID (UID) and full cluster-provisioning privileges, leading to arbitrary code execution.

HTTP::Session versions before 0.43 for Perl allow memcached command injection via unfiltered session ids in HTTP::Session::Store::Memcached.

The session id from the client's cookie reaches memcached unchanged as the cache key.

A CR and LF in the session id end the cache command early, and the server reads the bytes after them as further commands.

EveryDocs Core before 1.6.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to access other users' records through unscoped Model.find(params[:id]) lookups in multiple controllers. Self-registered attackers can enumerate sequential ids to read, modify, or delete other users' documents and stored files, and rename or delete their folders, tags and people.

WP File Manager before 8.0.7 contains a file upload restriction bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to upload arbitrary PHP files by exploiting a misconfigured elFinder connector in file_folder_manager.php where an empty uploadDeny list causes allowPutMime() to unconditionally return true, bypassing the uploadAllow restriction. Attackers can upload a .php file directly or upload it under an allowed filename and then rename it via the rename connector command, achieving remote code execution as the web server user.

Dell Enterprise Sonic Distribution, versions prior to 4.6.1, contains an OS Command Injection vulnerability. An unauthenticated adjacent network attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to arbitrary command execution. This vulnerability is considered critical as it may allow unauthenticated command execution.

Emitter through 3.1 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows any channel key holder to forge a master key because channel keys use bare XOR Salsa20 encryption without a MAC or signature. Attackers can flip the permissions byte to the master value and present the forged key to the keygen service to mint keys with arbitrary permissions on every channel of the contract.

Dockhand before 1.0.57 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows non-admin users with settings:edit permission to modify OIDC provider configuration due to an improper permission check. Attackers can send a PUT request to /api/auth/oidc/<provider-id> setting adminClaim to their own OIDC group, gaining full admin access on their next OIDC login.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in modplug_read_header() in libavformat/libmodplug.c that allocates the buffer using max_size instead of sz. When max_size is set to 0, attackers can supply crafted module files that avio_read() copies into a zero-sized buffer, causing memory corruption, crashes, or possible code execution.
Due to improper input validation, an authenticated remote attacker could execute arbitrary commands on the target system.

Rootways Authorize.net CIM Pro extension for Magento 2 before 4.1.5 contains an unauthenticated server-side request forgery vulnerability in the Apple Pay merchant validation controller. Attackers can supply file://, gopher://, or dict:// URLs in the validationUrl parameter to read app/etc/env.php credentials and encryption keys or reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.

A flaw was found in Foreman. A command injection vulnerability exists in the foreman-rake errors:fetch_log task. The request_id parameter is passed to an underlying system command (typically grep) without adequate shell neutralization. While the task is intended to fetch specific log entries, an attacker with sudo permissions to execute this rake task can inject shell metacharacters (such as ;, ", or |) to break out of the intended command and execute arbitrary code.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 remote code execution was possible via a file write bypass in the Kotlin DSL sandbox

A flaw was found in Foreman. The foreman-rake initialization logic in /usr/share/foreman/config/settings.rb contains a vulnerable code pattern where configuration data is processed through two distinct executable layers. This creates a multi-stage execution chain that allows for both Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) and insecure deserialization. This vulnerability can lead to remote code execution, total infrastructure compromise and supply chain risk.

A flaw was found in Eclipse Che che-machine-exec. This vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote arbitrary command execution and secret exfiltration (SSH keys, tokens, etc.) from other users' Developer Workspace containers, via an unauthenticated JSON-RPC / websocket API exposed on TCP port 3333.

A flaw was found in Foreman. A remote attacker could exploit a command injection vulnerability in Foreman's WebSocket proxy implementation. This vulnerability arises from the system's use of unsanitized hostname values from compute resource providers when constructing shell commands. By operating a malicious compute resource server, an attacker could achieve remote code execution on the Foreman server when a user accesses VM VNC console functionality. This could lead to the compromise of sensitive credentials and the entire managed infrastructure.

A flaw was found in camel-infinispan. This vulnerability involves unsafe deserialization in the ProtoStream remote aggregation repository. A remote attacker with low privileges could exploit this by sending specially crafted data, leading to arbitrary code execution. This allows the attacker to gain full control over the affected system, impacting its confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

A flaw was found in Foreman. The Red Hat Satellite /unattended/provision API endpoint is vulnerable to an authentication bypass due to a semantic logic flaw in host_verifier.rb. The application verifies the database state of a provisioning token rather than its actual presence in the incoming HTTP request. Because a host actively undergoing provisioning has an unexpired token in the database, the server's valid_host_token? method evaluates to true, granting access to the kickstart template even if the requester provides no token at all in the URL.
In Apache Airflow 1.8.2 and earlier, a CSRF vulnerability allowed for a remote command injection on a default install of Airflow.

Nexterm through 1.2.2-BETA contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows users with permissions.manage to gain unauthorized permissions because addGroupMember and setUserGroups lack the grantsBeyondCaller check. Attackers can add their own account to custom groups via the group membership endpoints to inherit permissions like users.impersonate and settings.backup.

IN THE EXTENSION SCRIPT, a SQL Injection vulnerability was found in PostgreSQL if it uses @extowner@, @extschema@, or @extschema:...@ inside a quoting construct (dollar quoting, '', or ""). If an administrator has installed files of a vulnerable, trusted, non-bundled extension, an attacker with database-level CREATE privilege can execute arbitrary code as the bootstrap superuser.

wishthis through 1.2.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in User::ownsWishlist() that allows authenticated users to modify other users' wishes and wishlists. Attackers can supply sequential wish_id and wishlist_id values to the wishes and wishlists API handlers to edit wishes, add wishes, or rename and delete wishlists.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to leverage pre-staged malicious content to conduct an XML injection attack due to insufficient parameter validation. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This is MTLVULN-1862.

Due to improper restriction, authenticated attackers could retrieve and read system files of the underlying server through the XML interface. The information that can be read can lead to a full system compromise.

Rapid7 Metasploit Framework versions prior to 6.5.10 suffer from an Improper Access Control issue in the msfdb database initialisation component whereby a PostgreSQL cluster initialised via msfdb init is configured with trust authentication and a world-accessible Unix domain socket in /tmp, allowing any local user on the same host to authenticate as the passwordless postgres superuser and execute arbitrary operating system commands as the msfdb owner. 


This issue is fixed in version 6.5.10.

openSIS 5.1 before 9.0 contains a local file inclusion vulnerability that allows authenticated users to include arbitrary files through the modname parameter of ajax.php. Attackers can prefix a payload with misc/ and use ../ directory traversal to read sensitive files like /etc/passwd or execute local scripts in the web server context. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

Fluxion before 6.39 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the fluxion.sh target scanner, which decodes access point ESSIDs with eval after escaping only single quotes. Attackers within Wi-Fi range can broadcast an access point with a crafted SSID to execute commands as root when the operator scans or selects it.

EUSurvey 1.4.4.6738 through 1.6, prior to commit de1145c, contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the public results page GET /publication/{shortname} that allows unauthenticated attackers to infer non-public response data. ReportingService builds a SQL column expression from part of a user-supplied filter parameter name and inserts it directly into the query, so a visitor to any survey that publishes its results can inject boolean conditions and use the presence or absence of public result rows to infer private reporting data, including response data and respondent metadata from other surveys.

A Server-Side Request Forgery and supply chain flaw was found in the OpenShift Console Helm catalog proxy. A namespace tenant can plant a ProjectHelmChartRepository with an arbitrary URL that the console pod fetches server-side, bypassing tenant egress restrictions. Combined with catalog metadata poisoning and admin-mediated chart installation, this enables privilege escalation.

mcp-ssh-manager is an MCP server for managing servers over SSH with human approval, an encrypted vault, and a live audit trail. Prior to 3.8.5, ssh_backup_create, ssh_backup_restore, ssh_backup_schedule, and ssh_backup_list build remote shell commands from caller-controlled values in src/backup-manager.js and inline backup handlers in src/index.js without neutralizing shell metacharacters. Crafted database, connection, backup directory, path, exclusion, schedule, or comment arguments can therefore execute arbitrary OS commands on managed remote servers as the configured SSH user. ssh_backup_schedule can persist execution through cron. ssh_backup_list does not pass through the server policy check and remains available in readonly and restricted modes, allowing command execution despite those restrictions. Tool arguments can be supplied by a malicious or compromised MCP client or steered through indirect prompt injection; fully trusted benign arguments do not trigger the issue. The earlier database-helper remediation for CVE-2026-77383 applied shell quoting to src/database-manager.js but did not cover these parallel backup builders. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.5.

A flaw was found in Ansible Automation Platform (AAP). Read-only scoped OAuth2 API Tokens in AAP, are enforced at the Gateway level for Gateway-specific operations. However, this vulnerability allows read-only tokens to perform write operations on backend services (e.g., Controller, Hub, EDA). If this flaw were exploited, an attacker‘s capabilities would only be limited by role based access controls (RBAC).

ioBroker.lovelace before 7.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the onCards() request handler that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to read arbitrary files via unsanitized dot-dot segments. Attackers can send crafted requests to the /cards/_static_/, /hacsfiles/, or /local/custom_ui/ routes to read files including ioBroker configuration and stored credentials.

GreaterWMS through 2.1.54 contains an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability in the css, js, statics and fonts routes in greaterwms/views.py, which concatenate raw request.path_info without normalization. Attackers can send URL-encoded ../ sequences to read db.sqlite3 and obtain user openid tokens, enabling impersonation of any account.

devpi-web before 5.2.0 contains an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability in the +doc documentation route because docs_file_exists and docs_file_path in doczip.py never confine relpath to the documentation directory. Attackers can request a relpath with a leading // or percent-encoded .. segments to read server files, including the keyfs sqlite database holding password hashes.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in its filesystem storage bucket that only canonicalizes the bucket root, not descendant symlinks. Attackers can reference paths through a pre-existing symlink inside the bucket that pass the lexical prefix check, reading and writing files across the host filesystem.

PLANET GS-5220-8P2T2S (hardware version 3.0) firmware versions before 3.2412b261008 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to corrupt stack memory by submitting an oversized webstax_auth HTTP Cookie value that is copied into a fixed-size stack buffer without length validation. Attackers can send a crafted unauthenticated HTTP request with an oversized cookie to overwrite the saved return address and corrupt stack memory, leading to memory corruption and potential denial of service on the device.

rConfig Core 8.0.0 before 8.2.17 and rConfig Pro before 8.4.0 contain a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Config Search View Matches dialog, which renders configuration context via v-html without escaping. Attackers can place markup in device banners, interface descriptions, ACL remarks or SNMP locations to execute script in a user's session and read stored configurations containing secrets.

A flaw was found in the Keycloak server's client management component. When a client is created or imported with authorization services enabled, the system fails to properly clear an internal session attribute used during the setup process. This allows an authenticated attacker with client management permissions to bypass security controls and upload a malicious JavaScript policy, which is then executed on the server when an authorization request is made. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to run arbitrary code on the server, potentially compromising the entire system.

OpenWrt LuCI luci-app-travelmate on master before 3.0.0-1, on openwrt-25.12 before 2.4.9-6, and on openwrt-24.10 and openwrt-23.05 (no fix available) grants file exec permissions for state-mutating commands in the read scope of its rpcd ACL, letting authenticated read-only users run those commands as root. Attackers can invoke ubus file exec on /etc/init.d/travelmate setup, start, stop, restart, or /sbin/ifup to modify and commit network and firewall configuration or disrupt the travelmate daemon.

Fleet from 4.71.0 before 4.88.2 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the SAML SSO callback that looks up sessions using unvalidated client-supplied identifiers. Users able to run live queries or enroll secret holders can plant attacker-controlled identity provider metadata in the session store, then present a self-signed SAML response to log in as a global admin.

A flaw was found in PostgreSQL that allows authenticated database users to execute arbitrary code through missing overflow checks during SQL array value modification. This issue exists due to an integer overflow during array modification where a remote user can trigger the overflow by providing specially crafted data. This enables the execution of arbitrary code on the target system, allowing users to write arbitrary bytes to memory and extensively read the server's memory.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix use-after-free in oplock break notification

smb2_oplock_break_noti() reads opinfo->conn without any lock and
dereferences it after two allocations which may sleep.  When the
durable handle owning the oplock is disconnected, session_fd_check()
clears opinfo->conn and drops its conn reference under ci->m_lock, and
the last ksmbd_conn_put() frees the connection.  A break triggered by
another connection that races with the teardown can then resurrect the
freed connection: ksmbd_conn_get() is a plain atomic_inc, and the
queued break work later dereferences the stale conn via
ksmbd_conn_write(), a use-after-free reachable by any authenticated
client holding a durable batch oplock.

Thread the caller's inode into the notification path instead of taking
a new reference on it.  Every caller of oplock_break() already holds a
live ksmbd_file (or an explicit ksmbd_inode_lookup_lock() reference,
in the parent lease break paths) on the inode that owns the break
target's oplock list, so ci cannot be freed during the call, and its
lock can be taken without dereferencing opinfo->o_fp, which a
concurrent close may free.  Select and pin the connection under
ci->m_lock, the same lock session_fd_check() and
ksmbd_reopen_durable_fd() use to update opinfo->conn, so a concurrent
detach either loses the race to the clear or keeps the connection
alive until the notification work releases it.  Transfer the reference
to the work item and release it on allocation failures.

A flaw was found in Foreman. This vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker with low-level read permissions to achieve arbitrary code execution on the underlying server. By manipulating the permitted methods list within the template rendering engine, an attacker can bypass the safemode sandbox isolation and execute unauthorized commands directly on the host system.

TridotsTech go1cms master branch through commit 7f68d05 and version-3 branch before commit ead8da3 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the guest-whitelisted update_doc method that allows unauthenticated attackers to modify any document. Attackers can supply a doctype, name and arbitrary fields that are saved with ignore_permissions=True, altering User records to escalate privileges, take over accounts or tamper with business data.

BZFlag bzfs before 2.4.32 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in NetHandler::tcpReceive() that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to corrupt heap memory by sending a TCP message with a body length of exactly 1024. Attackers can overwrite the tcplen receive offset with a negative value to write controlled bytes before the buffer, crashing the server or executing commands as the bzfs user.

open62541 Subscription Use-After-Free Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of open62541. Authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of subscriptions. The issue results from the lack of validating the existence of an object prior to performing operations on the object. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the service account. Was ZDI-CAN-30231.

OwnTracks Recorder before 1.0.5 contains a format string vulnerability in json_response() and related output functions that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute code by storing a malicious tid value. Attackers can publish locations via POST /pub or MQTT with printf specifiers in tid, then read them back through GET /api/0/last to leak addresses and write memory.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 remote code execution was possible via native code loading in the Kotlin DSL sandbox
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 remote code execution was possible via Mercurial repository contents

In HandleEndTransaction of bearer.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a missing check that the object still exists after a security upgrade callback completes synchronously. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In ProcessWriteQueue of client.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a callback that continues to use its object after the object is destroyed during connection shutdown. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In StartA2dpOffload of a2dp_offload_manager.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a stored callback that is not cleared when the link it refers to is destroyed. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In SignalError of logical_link.cc, there is a possible use after free due to an error callback that can destroy the object while its channel list is still being iterated. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.
Tanium addressed an unauthorized code execution vulnerability in the Tanium Default Content.

Community Store for Concrete CMS before 2.8.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script via the order email in single_pages/dashboard/store/orders.php. Attackers can place guest orders with quoted email local parts containing markup to execute script in a store manager's session when viewing the order.

Grav Form plugin 1.1.0 before 9.1.40 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in Form::uploadFiles(), which sanitizes SVG only when a file's last extension is .svg and accepts markup under unrecognized extensions. Anonymous attackers can upload files like drawing.svg.foo through public any-type upload forms, running script in an administrator's session when opened, enabling super-admin creation on Grav 2.x with Admin2.

The ggml-rpc server suffers from an uninitialized heap memory disclosure vulnerability where the alloc_buffer function provides new clients with buffers containing stale data from previously freed allocations. This allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to perform an in-bounds read via get_tensor to recover sensitive information, such as model weights or KV-cache data, belonging to other clients sharing the same server.
In Apache Airflow, prior to version 2.2.4, some example DAGs did not properly sanitize user-provided params, making them susceptible to OS Command Injection from the web UI.

A flaw was found in the file-xmc plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted XMC image file, the plugin does not properly validate the comment subtype before using it as an array index. This missing validation leads to out-of-bounds memory access, invalid free and use-after-free issues. This vulnerability can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

A flaw was found in rubyipmi, a gem used in the Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) component of Red Hat Satellite. An authenticated attacker with host creation or update permissions could exploit this vulnerability by crafting a malicious username for the BMC interface. This could lead to remote code execution (RCE) on the system.

An improper input validation flaw was found in the eBPF subsystem in the Linux kernel. The issue occurs due to a lack of proper validation of dynamic pointers within user-supplied eBPF programs prior to executing them. This may allow an attacker with CAP_BPF privileges to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of the kernel.

An integer overflow flaw was found in the SASL I/O layer of 389 Directory Server (389-ds-base). In sasl_io_start_packet(), adding sizeof(uint32_t) to a crafted SASL packet length prefix of 0xFFFFFFFC causes unsigned wraparound to zero, bypassing the nsslapd-maxsasliosize limit and leading to a heap buffer overflow of up to approximately 2 megabytes of attacker-controlled data. After a successful SASL bind with integrity protection (SSF > 0), a remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE). In FreeIPA and Red Hat Identity Management deployments, any domain user with a valid Kerberos ticket, enrolled host, or service account can trigger this vulnerability over the network. This flaw is independent of CVE-2025-14905, which patched schema.c only and did not modify sasl_io.c.

A flaw was found in the Multicluster Engine for Kubernetes ClusterCurator controller. A tenant administrator with namespace-scoped privileges can exploit this vulnerability by creating a namespaced ClusterCurator. This action inadvertently grants the tenant administrator the ability to mint a token for a ServiceAccount with cluster-wide administrative authority. This leads to a privilege escalation, allowing the tenant administrator to gain full control over the cluster.

A heap buffer overflow flaw was found in the SASL I/O layer of 389 Directory Server (389-ds-base). In sasl_io_start_packet(), the wrapped-record length read from the wire is validated only against an upper bound. A small wire length (0, 1, or 2) produces an encrypted_buffer_count below the already-consumed encrypted_buffer_offset, causing an unsigned subtraction underflow in sasl_io_read_packet(). PR_Recv is then requested to read approximately 4 GiB into a 1024-byte heap buffer, resulting in a heap buffer overflow with attacker-controlled content. After a successful SASL bind with integrity protection (SSF > 0), a remote authenticated attacker can cause a denial of service or potentially achieve remote code execution. This flaw is distinct from CVE-2026-11774, whose fix only guards against upper-bound overflow.

A flaw was found in the X.Org X server and Xwayland when processing X11 Present extension notifications. Improper error handling during notification creation can leave dangling pointers that lead to a use-after-free condition. This can cause memory corruption or a crash, potentially allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service.

A vulnerability was found in Perl. This security issue occurs while Perl for Windows relies on the system path environment variable to find the shell (`cmd.exe`). When running an executable that uses the Windows Perl interpreter, Perl attempts to find and execute `cmd.exe` within the operating system. However, due to path search order issues, Perl initially looks for cmd.exe in the current working directory. This flaw allows an attacker with limited privileges to place`cmd.exe` in locations with weak permissions, such as `C:\ProgramData`. By doing so, arbitrary code can be executed when an administrator attempts to use this executable from these compromised locations.

A flaw was found in the 389-ds-base server. A heap buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the `schema_attr_enum_callback` function within the `schema.c` file. This occurs because the code incorrectly calculates the buffer size by summing alias string lengths without accounting for additional formatting characters. When a large number of aliases are processed, this oversight can lead to a heap overflow, potentially allowing a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE).

A flaw was found in ansible-core. The ansible-galaxy role install command processes dependency specifications from a role's meta/requirements.yml file. Due to improper neutralization of argument delimiters, a malicious role author can inject arbitrary git configuration flags through the src field. This allows arbitrary code execution on the machine of a user who installs the role via ansible-galaxy role install.

A flaw was found in Foreman. The Usergroup model in Foreman does not properly validate role assignments against the calling user's permissions. This allows an authenticated user with usergroup management permissions to attach arbitrary roles, including administrative roles, to a user group and then add themselves as a member. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability leads to full privilege escalation, granting the attacker administrator-level access.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ptp: vmclock: prevent read-only mappings from becoming writable

vmclock_miscdev_mmap() rejects writable mappings of the shared vmclock
ABI page with -EROFS, but leaves VM_MAYWRITE set.  Userspace can map the
page read-only and then upgrade it to writable with mprotect(), after
which the guest can corrupt the host-written timekeeping data (sequence
counter, UTC time, TSC offset) that the vmclock ABI defines as read-only.

Clear VM_MAYWRITE on the read-only path so the mapping cannot be
upgraded, as i915 does for its read-only objects and as fixed in drm/vc4
(CVE-2026-68445) and drm/panthor (CVE-2024-53071).

A flaw was found in rpm. An attacker can supply a crafted manifest file that, when processed by a user or automation using `rpm -q -p` or similar manifest-processing flows, leads to arbitrary code execution. This occurs because manifest entries are unexpectedly macro-expanded before being opened, allowing embedded shell commands to run with the privileges of the `rpm` process. Successful exploitation can lead to a full compromise of confidentiality, integrity, and availability for the affected account.

virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.7.13, the generated activate (bash and zsh) and activate.fish scripts place values already escaped by shlex.quote inside an additional quoted context. In the bash and zsh script, a crafted virtual environment path reaches __VIRTUAL_ENV__ when a relocated environment's recorded directory is absent; in the fish script, crafted Tcl or Tk library paths reach __TCL_LIBRARY__ or __TK_LIBRARY__. The surplus quotes can terminate the data-only quoted run and leave shell metacharacters parsed as commands when a user sources the activation script, allowing code execution with that user's privileges. This issue is fixed in version 21.7.13.

A flaw was found in GIMP. The PSD thumbnail resource loader performs a BGR-to-RGB channel swap with a fixed 3-byte stride and does not verify that the JPEG thumbnail is RGB. A crafted grayscale PSD thumbnail can cause a heap out-of-bounds read and write in the plug-in process, leading to a crash and potentially arbitrary code execution when the victim browses or opens the file.

A flaw was found in GIMP. The XCF loader can leave a dangling pointer in the linked-channels list when a linked channel is later destroyed via a selection property. Opening a crafted XCF file can cause a use-after-free in the main GIMP process, leading to a crash and potentially arbitrary code execution.

A flaw was found in GIMP. Opening a crafted XCF that selects a path and then fails to load that path can cause a use-after-free in the main process, leading to a crash and potentially arbitrary code execution.

A vulnerability has been identified in Rexroth IndraWorks. This flaw allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the user’s system by parsing a manipulated file, because the file parser fails to properly sanitize the path name(s) or references embedded in the manipulated file. Exploitation requires user interaction, specifically opening a specially crafted file, which then causes the application to traverse outside the target directory and to write files in unauthorized locations, eventually enabling Remote Code Execution (RCE). This can lead to a complete compromise of the system running Rexroth IndraWorks.

HyperFrames before 0.9.30 contains a missing Origin and Host validation vulnerability in the unauthenticated Studio API that allows malicious web pages to write project files. Attackers can send CORS-simple POST requests to /api/projects/:id/files/* or use DNS rebinding to plant package.json scripts or agent configs, leading to command execution.

Bonsai through 6.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated Editor users to access admin pages because AdminAuthHandler accepts both Administrator and Editor roles. Attackers can use UsersController and DynamicConfigController to reset administrator passwords, promote accounts to Administrator, and change global settings to take over the instance.

UrlHub before 1.20.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to create accounts via the POST /admin/user/store route because role:admin middleware only covers view and create actions. Attackers, including self-registered users, can submit a request with role=admin to create an administrator account and gain full administrative control.

ArtisanCloud PowerX through 1.0.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the IAM role management API that allows authenticated tenant members to escalate privileges. Attackers holding even the lowest built-in role can call the permissions/grant-ids, permissions/grant, or bind/member routes to grant permissions or bind privileged roles, gaining tenant administrative access.
Privilege escalation due to incorrect boundary conditions in the Graphics: CanvasWebGL component on Android. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 160.0.1 and Thunderbird 161.

KDE Gwenview PNG File Parsing Integer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of KDE Gwenview. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of PNG files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in an integer overflow before allocating a buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-29373.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 privilege escalation was possible via username handling in token authentication

codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.0, automatic import of a repository's .codebase-memory/ artifact allocated a decompression buffer using the attacker-controlled 64-bit original_size value from artifact.json but truncated that value to int when passing the destination capacity to the Zstandard decompressor. A value with bit 31 set became negative and was sign-extended to a large size_t, allowing the decompressor to write frame content beyond the actual allocation. Indexing a malicious repository containing the crafted artifact could corrupt heap memory with attacker-controlled bytes, causing a reliable crash and potentially code execution. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

EUSurvey 1.5.5 through 1.6, prior to commit d5295d5, contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the POST /forms/bulkchange endpoint that allows any authenticated user to take over or delete other users' surveys. SurveyController accepts arbitrary survey IDs and privilege values, and BulkExecutor applies the requested access-right changes or deletion without checking whether the requester can manage those surveys, allowing an ordinary ROLE_USER account to grant itself full control of another user's survey, read its draft and results, edit the form, manage its invitations, or delete it.
Privilege escalation due to integer overflow in the Graphics: WebGPU component. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161, and Thunderbird 153.8.
Privilege escalation due to use-after-free in the Graphics component. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 115.46, Firefox ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161, and Thunderbird 153.8.

Privilege escalation due to incorrect boundary conditions in the Audio/Video: Playback component. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 115.46, Firefox ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161, and Thunderbird 153.8.

Privilege escalation due to use-after-free in the Networking: Cache component. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 115.46, Firefox ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161, and Thunderbird 153.8.

Privilege escalation due to incorrect boundary conditions in the Layout: Text and Fonts component. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 115.46, Firefox ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161, and Thunderbird 153.8.

A flaw was found in the OpenShift console. Unauthenticated access to the `/api/devfile/` and `/api/devfile/samples/` endpoints allows a remote attacker to send crafted devfile payloads. This can lead to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), where the console pod makes requests to internal services and reflects partial responses to the attacker. Additionally, by sending repeated large requests without a specified content length, an attacker can cause unbounded memory growth, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

An OS Command Injection vulnerability affecting Station Launcher App in 3DEXPERIENCE platform from Release 3DEXPERIENCE R2023x through Release 3DEXPERIENCE R2026x could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands on the server.

An OS Command Injection vulnerability affecting Station Launcher App in 3DEXPERIENCE platform from Release 3DEXPERIENCE R2023x through Release 3DEXPERIENCE R2026x could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands on the server.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 remote code execution was possible via Subversion VCS root settings
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 remote code execution was possible via Mercurial VCS root settings
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 remote code execution was possible via build access codes disclosed to project users
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 remote code execution was possible via Mercurial subrepository paths
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 remote code execution was possible via personal builds with versioned settings

OS command injection in the a3cli restricted shell in Lantronix S2220 Series 2 allows an authenticated attacker to bypass shell restrictions and execute arbitrary operating system commands via unsanitized command substitution metacharacters, including backticks and $(), in parameters of permitted commands over SSH. This vulnerability is fixed in firmware version 1.3.37.

A heap-buffer-overflow vulnerability exists in the APNG (Animated PNG) file loader of GIMP. This flaw occurs when the `fcTL` width exceeds the `IHDR` width, leading to pixel data being written past the end of a heap allocation. Additionally, a heap-based buffer overflow exists in the DDS plug-in due to a BPP mismatch in the `load_layer()` function. Both vulnerabilities can be triggered by opening a specially crafted image file, potentially leading to code execution.

U-Boot versions 2025.07 before 2026.10-rc5 contain a use-after-free vulnerability in the httpc_recv_cb() function within the lwIP wget implementation. When HTTP data storage fails, the callback frees the connection PCB but returns ERR_BUF instead of ERR_ABRT, causing the TCP input path to access released memory and crash the bootloader.

paicoding from commit b8206b9 through commit 903adce uses predictable credentials for accounts created via ZSXQ login, because loginByZsxq derives both the username and password solely from the member's ZSXQ number. Unauthenticated attackers can read that number from the victim's /user/{userId} profile page, compute the credentials, and log in via /login/username to take over the account.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 remote code execution was possible via class injection in the Kotlin DSL sandbox
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 remote code execution was possible via Kotlin DSL compiler arguments

node-soap before 1.14.1 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in WSDL.xmlToObject that allows unauthenticated attackers to pollute Object.prototype via an XML element with id="__proto__". Attackers can send a single crafted SOAP request to a soap.listen() server, or return a malicious response to a client, causing all subsequent SOAP parsing to fail until process restart.
Server-side request forgery in Profile Data Roaming Service (PDRS) allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.
Server-side request forgery in Azure Machine Learning allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.
Tanium addressed an unauthorized code execution vulnerability in the Tanium Default Content.

A race condition was found in the QXL driver in the Linux kernel. The qxl_mode_dumb_create() function dereferences the qobj returned by the qxl_gem_object_create_with_handle(), but the handle is the only one holding a reference to it. This flaw allows an attacker to guess the returned handle value and trigger a use-after-free issue, potentially leading to a denial of service or privilege escalation.

rsync before 3.5.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the delta-transfer sender's hash_search() in match.c that allows malicious receivers to trigger unbounded strong-checksum work at consecutive offsets. Unauthenticated attackers pulling from a public daemon module can supply weak checksums colliding with consecutive rolling windows plus non-matching strong checksums, exhausting sender CPU across concurrent connections.

Fleet before 4.86.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server memory through quadratic XML canonicalization of unsigned SAML responses. Attackers can send a single crafted SAML response with deeply nested elements declaring new namespace prefixes to POST /api/v1/fleet/sso/callback, crashing the Fleet server.

Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows remote attackers to forge privileged actions such as administrator user creation by merging $_GET and $_POST parameters without requiring an anti-CSRF token. Attackers can craft a malicious link or auto-navigating page that issues a plain GET request, exploiting the lack of CSRF protection and SameSite=Lax cookie behavior on top-level navigations to create unauthorized administrator accounts.

Kanbanz by Softaculous plugin for WordPress before 1.0.3 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows authenticated Kanban Staff users to access and modify boards they are not members of by exploiting admin-ajax handlers that fail to call kanbanz_user_can_access_board() or per-task edit checks on attacker-supplied board_id or task_id parameters. Attackers can supply arbitrary board IDs to read sensitive task data, overwrite status columns, subtasks, and labels, inject comments, upload or delete attachments, and create tasks or set WIP limits on boards owned by other teams.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Compiler).  Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u511b33-perf, 17.0.21.0.3, 21.0.13.0.3, 25.0.5.0.3, 27.0.1.0.3; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.21.0.3 and  21.0.13.0.3; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.20.0.3. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Note: This vulnerability can only be exploited by supplying data to APIs in the specified Component without using Untrusted Java Web Start applications or Untrusted Java applets, such as through a web service.
